Sweetwater has had some incredible deals during its sale, but one discount has caught my eye in particular. The already super-affordable Walrus Audio Fundamental pedal series just got even cheaper, taking most of the series down to just $79!

I love the Fundamental series so much. They look cool, are simple to use, and, more importantly, sound incredible. We even named the Reverb as one of our top picks in our best reverb pedals guide, and that was before it had over $20 knocked off the retail price!
Of course, you can save on more than just the reverb model, with delay and modulation effects also included in the sale.

Fundamental Series Reverb: was $99.99 now $70
An easy first recommendation is the Fundamental Reverb pedal, a stompbox that we have a lot of love for, and one that features as one of our picks for the best reverb pedals available right now. It takes the slot of the best reverb for beginners on our list because of just how simple it is to use, with three different modes – hall, spring, and plate – and three sliders controlling Decay, Tone, and Mix, respectively. I should make it clear: it's not just for beginners. Anybody looking for a natural reverb, without any unnecessary complexity, should seriously consider it, particularly when it sits at just $79.00.View Deal

Fundamental Series Delay: was $99.99 now $70
As DSP power has advanced, many delay pedals have become supremely powerful, but equally confusing and complicated to use. I just want a delay pedal that sounds great and is simple to use – enter the Fundamental Delay. It has three sliders to set the parameters of the effect – Time, Feedback, and Mix – and three different modes: digital, analog, and reverse. Hold down the footswitch, and you've got tap tempo too, which for me makes this basically the perfect delay pedal, offering just enough variety and functionality while remaining a breeze to operate.View Deal

Fundamental Series Chorus: was $99.99 now $70
No collection of top choices from Walrus Audio would be complete without some kind of modulation effect, and my favorite from the Fundamental series is the Chorus, which is now just $79.00 at Sweetwater. With the same consistent setup of three sliders and three modes - light, medium, and heavy - it's utterly effortless to get great, lush guitar tones. One thing that's great about this whole lineup is the top-mounted input and output jacks, making the pedals space-efficient on your board.View Deal

Given Jack White’s slightly elusive and incredibly hip reputation, when it comes time for a partnership between his Third Man Hardware brand and another pedal company, you’d be forgiven for expecting him to team up with an underground builder for something equally exclusive.
Not so. Because for the Triple Threat, Mr W has thrown his hat into the ring with Donner, a Chinese brand specializing in affordable gear.

The Triple Threat houses three analog pedals in a single aluminum chassis. These circuits are based on Donner’s own effects pedals, including the Pearl Tremor phaser and Yellow Fall delay, with the form factor borrowed from its Alpha Cruncher multi-effects, and White and Third Man beefing up the components to ensure better sound and sturdier build quality.

The Third Man Hardware x Donner Triple Threat packs three analog effects – distortion, phaser, and echo – into one compact pedal. Designed in collaboration with Jack White, it's a versatile addition to any pedalboard, delivering everything from gritty garage-rock tones to psychedelic textures. View Deal
If you're looking for a solid distortion pedal at a killer price this Black Friday, you won't go wrong with 13% off the legendary ProCo Rat.
Launched in 1988, the Rat 2 has become one of the most notable distortion boxes on the market, famed for its tonal flexibility and versatile blend of overdrive, distortion, and fuzz.

The list of Rat pedal fans is pretty long and impressive, including classic rockers like Jeff Beck, David Gilmour, Joe Perry, Andy Summers, Kurt Cobain, Dave Grohl, Buzz Osborne, Graham Coxon, Frank Black, James Hetfield, Rivers Cuomo, and so many more.
I've had a Rat on my board from time to time, too. It was actually one of the first pedals I ever bought with my pocket money when I was a kid just starting out!

Rat: was $72.99 now $63.51

When you talk about iconic overdrive stompboxes, the Klon Centaur sits right at the top of the heap. Everyone from John Mayer to Jeff Beck has leaned on this circuit, building up a massive cult following over the decades.

Because Bill Finnegan only built around 8,000 units between 1994 and 2008, hunting down an original will cost you a small fortune on the used market. Players go crazy for it because it nails that sweet, natural breakup of a pushed tube amp without blowing out your windows.

Since original units are practically unobtainable for most of us, plenty of builders have tried to recreate the magic. Out of all the clones on the market, Warm Audio's Centavo is the one that actually lives on my personal pedalboard. Seeing Guitar Center knock a hefty $80 off the price tag was too good to pass up without spreading the word.

WA-CV Centavo: was $179 now $99
This pedal combines the classic aesthetics of the famed Klon Centaur with an impressive sound that makes it a top contender among Klon clones - and a firm favorite among us at Guitar World. Save $90 at Guitar Center. View Deal

When I reviewed the entire Marshall pedal range last year, I said, "The legendary amp maker is taking aim at other Marshall-in-a-box pedals with a new lineup that is diverse, well-made, and very well-thought-out. Okay, they are on the heavy side, and we'd prefer them to be a little smaller, but it can't be denied that no one knows the iconic Marshall tone better than Marshall themselves."
Right now you can score 30% off the entire range at Guitar Center, bringing the price down to only $129.99.
If you want my personal recommendation, I'd go for the JCM800 model.
Look, I love the Big Muff. Genuinely, it's my favorite pedal ever made.

If you think about it, the Big Muff Pi is kind of like the Godzilla of fuzz pedals. It’s huge, unstoppable, and has enough gain to level a city. Okay, sure, it takes up half your pedalboard, but with tone this good, who cares?
If you want to sound like a guitar legend and don’t mind sacrificing space, I think the Muff’s atomic roar is worth every inch.

Yes, more feature-packed or compact fuzz pedals are on the market, and some variants offer greater flexibility, but none capture the iconic sound and spirit of the original quite like the Big Muff Pi. If you want classic fuzz in its purest form, this pedal remains the gold standard.View Deal

When Tech 21 released the SansAmp PSA-1 in 1993, it completely revolutionized the industry, becoming a studio and stage staple. However, as certain core components became unavailable over time, Tech 21 was forced to retire it.

It retains the same all-analog circuitry, with the programming and memory sections upgraded to digital. This new-and-improved version lets you record direct, use it as a preamp or outboard processor, and even operate it as a three-channel stompbox thanks to its Performance mode.
Safe to say, it's a powerhouse addition to your toolkit – and it's down to just $129 this Cyber Weekend.

Want the legendary tones of a studio rack unit in a pedalboard-friendly format? The Tech 21 SansAmp PSA 2.0 packs its iconic analog preamp circuitry into a programmable stompbox, with 49 factory presets, 128 memory locations, and plenty of tonal flexibility. From subtle breakup to full-blown high-gain distortion, it's a studio and stage-ready powerhouse. View Deal

It's easy to use without having to pore over a manual, and its screen makes navigating your loops a breeze, showing you exactly where you are in the recording. It's also compact, with plenty of memory for storing loops.
I mean, what else do you need, really?

Sweetwater is offering a bundle package with a $20 saving. For $649, you get the Nano Cortex and a mini expression pedal. Quite literally all you need for a professional fly rig.

When I went to Guitar Summit a few months ago, I had my first in-person encounter with the Knife Drop – the crazy Third Man Hardware x Eventide pedal that was co-masterminded by today's pre-eminent effects experimentalist, Jack White.

And I ain't kidding when I tell you it left my genuinely agog (and that's not a word I use very often). I can't even begin to think of a pedal that compares to it. It's a sub-octave fuzz pedal with synth flavors thrown in for good measure. I left Mannheim wanting one, and now Sweetwater has taken $29.90 off its asking price, I might pull the trigger.
At $255.65, it's still a sizable investment, but the Knife Drop is more for specialist 'boards, and there really isn't a pedal out there that does anything remotely similar.

GW's online EIC Mike did a stupendous job of doing it justice when he got to play through Jack White's entire pedalboard (only slightly jealous). Check out the video above to see it in action, but be warned: it will make you want to buy one.

If you're looking for a personal recommendation, here's one from me. I've been using the Eventide Knife Drop, made in conjunction with Jack White's Third Man Hardware, on my pedalboard for the last year or so. It delivers some seriously wild synth guitar tones, with an additional octave-up and octave-down tones. Unpredictable and totally unique, it's got a nice $29.90 discount in the sale.View Deal

I know what you're thinking: "An acoustic guitar overdrive? Are you having a laugh?" Well, nope, I'm not. I was skeptical at first as well, but it turns out this here Smolder OD from Fender is the real deal.

It's the only pedal that hasn't left my bandmates 'board, and it is the one effect he swears by. In fact, it's the driving force behind our live sound: a regular electric overdrive just feels fluffy and unfocussed with an acoustic, and lacks the clarity one needs.

The Smolder is specifically tailored with acoustics in mind, giving you a bit of National-esque crunch and bite when your acoustic needs a bit more tonal angst. Sweetwater has it discounted at $168.26, so I have sent it to my bandmate in case he wants a back up.
I'd recommend giving it a go if you felt mildly intrigued. You never know, it might change the way you play your acoustic...

If you are predominantly an acoustic player, I'd seriously think about giving this a go. A dedicated acoustic overdrive that won't make your tone sound spitty or messy, the Smolder does a perfect job of adding a bit of tailored grit and angst when those progressions need a bit of va-va-voom. There are loads of controls as well for fine-tuning, and light-up position markers on the knobs is a nice touch for darker stages.View Deal
